study: Joint MMLU PE-EmbPT and GittinsEval comparison

task.arm_order: arm_index = 100 * model_index + prompt_index, with zero-based indices
task.scope_note: The replay ranks model-prompt pairs jointly. The original PromptEval experiment ranked prompts separately within each model.

arm_features.prompt_transformation: Subject-level PCA features from the archived PromptEval covariates, shared across the 15 model rows for each template

bai.arm_sampling: Choose uniformly among least-sampled active arms using the seeded stratified sampler
bai.recommendation: Choose the highest-scoring active arm at each phase, with NumPy argmax on the current active-arm order
bai.elimination: Remove ceil(active_arm_count / 2) arms by ascending score using the historical NumPy argsort
bai.phase_scope_note: The pooled replay caps the upstream ceil(log2(K)) rule at five phases. The uncapped formula would give 11 phases for K = 1500. Upstream uses the observed empirical mean among survivors for the final recommendation.

fitting.data: Only binary responses observed by the end of the phase, including responses collected from arms eliminated earlier

logistic_39.score: X39 arm score, excluding the common constant
logistic_39.question_sampling: Uniform among unseen questions for the chosen arm

rasch39_random.model: Joint-task PE-EmbPT adaptation with question effects
rasch39_random.question_features: N identity columns for the N question IDs, shared across all 1,500 arms in the subject
rasch39_random.logit: X39 arm score + question easiness coefficient
rasch39_random.score: Average across N questions, using observed outcomes for seen cells and fitted sigmoid probabilities for unseen cells
rasch39_random.question_sampling: Uniform among unseen questions for the chosen arm

rasch39_balanced.model: Same fit and score as rasch39_random
rasch39_balanced.question_sampling: Uniform among the chosen arm's least-covered unseen questions, using question counts over all arms including eliminated arms

gittins.source: Supplied Figure 3 per-subject LCB caches for 19 subjects, 20 runs per subject, method, and cost mode
gittins.recommendation: Posterior mean minus posterior standard deviation

metric_and_budgets.metric: Raw simple regret = best full-matrix arm mean - recommended arm's full-matrix mean
metric_and_budgets.exhaustive_price_weighted_cost: N * sum of per-arm quoted input-token price weights
metric_and_budgets.x_percent_exhaustive: 100 * actual cumulative observations or price-weighted spend / matching subject denominator
metric_and_budgets.bai_price_view: Reprice the same unit-budget trajectories using per-model input-token quotes as relative weights
metric_and_budgets.prior_figure_axis: The original Figure 3 group cache mapped each Gittins run's first and last recorded spend to 0 and 1 before plotting it on a nominal 0%-10% scale

reporting.gittins_interpolation: Linear interpolation of each per-subject mean only inside its contiguous raw-budget interval with all 20 contributing runs
reporting.gittins_cohort_end: Earliest subject full-coverage endpoint within each cohort and method, capped at 10%. Ends at about 9.97%-10%
reporting.bai_interpolation: Use the latest completed phase at or before the requested budget. Carry final recommendations forward through 10%
reporting.aggregate_coverage: Require 20 seeds for every cohort subject. Subject BAI tables separately retain available-case means and seed counts
reporting.aggregation: Average seeds within subjects, then weight subjects equally
reporting.uncertainty: Mean plus or minus one sample standard error across subject means
reporting.paired_bai_contrasts: Pair available seeds within subject first, then average the per-subject mean differences equally
reporting.checkpoint_note: At unit cost, 9.9% uses the 8% BAI recommendation, and 10% includes the final phase
reporting.vertical_scale: Piecewise linear display expands raw regret below 0.05 to 65% of the positive axis height
reporting.curve_statistics: The CSVs retain raw regret. Checkpoint comparison counts are descriptive
reporting.replot_scope: Regenerate the figures from bundled CSVs without running the experiments
